dialect.detail: IBM DB2 mainframe COBOL; uses EXEC SQL with DB2-specific syntax including VALUE(), COALESCE(), CHAR(), CURRENT DATE arithmetic, INCLUDE SQLCA, and SCM schema references typical of IBM DB2 on z/OS
evidence: EXEC SQL DECLARE EMPCURS CURSOR FOR
INCLUDE EMPROACT, INCLUDE ACT, INCLUDE EMP
ORGANIZATION IS INDEXED with FILE STATUS

purpose.domain_detail: Employee payroll and project activity reporting using IBM DB2 tables (EMP, EMPPROJACT, ACT); reads an indexed VSAM file of employee data, inserts/updates DB2 tables, then produces a printed report of employee salary and project assignment information
purpose.summary: This batch COBOL program reads an indexed employee data file, deletes and re-inserts employee and project activity records into DB2 tables (SCM.EMP, SCM.EMPPROJACT), then uses a DB2 cursor to fetch and print a formatted report of employee names, departments, salaries, hire dates, and project assignments. It also computes and prints aggregate statistics (count, avg, min, max salary) for recently hired employees.

notable_features: DECLARE CURSOR with complex JOIN and CASE expression
EXEC SQL INCLUDE for SQLCA and host structure copybooks
ORGANIZATION IS INDEXED VSAM file with RECORD IS VARYING
OCCURS DEPENDING ON (ODO) for variable-length records
Formatted print report with dollar-sign edited PIC clauses ($$,$$$,999.99)
DB2 VALUE() and COALESCE() scalar functions
verdict.notes: Program authored by 'BRANDON PAXTON' with program-id CBL00 and a title line referencing 'KC03AF5' suggesting a course assignment identifier. The logic has some oddities (EMPCURS is opened twice - once in 100-HSK and again in 110-WRITE-DATA) and the 110-WRITE-DATA paragraph opens the cursor on every call rather than fetching sequentially, which is a student-level bug. Overall structure is consistent with a university DB2/COBOL programming course exercise.
